findings.premise: Sparse sibling relations and parent gather are sufficient to avoid quadratic fragment-pair work in quality review.
findings.evidence: The LLD promises to 'avoid new quadratic fragment-pair generation'. However, modelDimensionAdapter always adds compareStage and pairStage for quality. compareStage takes every described atom in later chunks, without checking parent identity or relations; compareCalls uses `firsts.flatMap(a => seconds.map(b => compareCall(a, b, execution)))`. Fragmenting one file therefore introduces cross-chunk sibling comparisons independently of sparse material connectivity, with potentially quadratic comparison work and candidates. findings.premise: Existing redivision can recover whenever a divisible diff fragment exceeds a lower effective limit or a reduced refusal budget.
findings.evidence: planChunks treats each atom as indivisible and executes `if (alone > hard) throw new AtomTooLargeError(...)`. job.redivide only repacks the same atom IDs. Meanwhile buildDiffSymbols accepts only DiffResult, before runDimensionJob computes the provider-aware effective limit. An allowed 16384-character span cannot fit a 12000-character cap even when smaller source spans would fit; existing redivision cannot repair that. The LLD specifies no budget-aware partitioning or provenance-preserving fragment subdivision seam. findings.premise: The design explicitly detects unsupported bounded execution, incomplete parent evidence and late/cancelled results before publishing completion.
findings.evidence: The proposed contracts require advertised boundedStructuredInput support, terminal unsupported-bounded-input handling, exact per-fragment note ownership and complete parent coverage. They also require pre/post-call and final-publication deadline checks plus owned shutdown. These are necessary extensions: driver.classify currently treats unrecognized errors as transient, gather has a generic NO_EVIDENCE branch, and runner finalization currently lacks a last signal/deadline check.
